category_title: Pupils with persistent disruptive and aggressive/abusive behavior
minimal_context: The student is participating in a weekly support group meeting and is asked to use their diary to reflect on a recent conflict.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at your support group diary and reflect on the conflict that happened yesterday. Can you tell me what the gains and losses were from that situation?

STUDENT: Why do I have to do this? It wasn't my mistake. He was deliberately doing things to annoy me.

TUTOR: We still need to talk about your reaction. Why did you get so angry?

STUDENT: I don't know! I don't understand why I behave in the ways that I do. You're always just trying to blame me.

TUTOR: You just need to calm down and try to control your behavior when we discuss these things.

STUDENT: (Loses temper) I can't control my behaviour when I want to! And I definitely can't control my behaviour when under pressure from you!

options.A: Leave the student free to choose any format and materials they like to complete the support group diary reflection.
options.B: Announce the duration of 45 or 60 minutes at the beginning of the session and use exactly the same phrasing each time (e.g., 'Today you have 60 minutes to reflect').
options.C: Allow the student to check out a preferred device to read after completing their support group diary reflection.
options.D: Use collaborative activities (scenarios, card sorts, prioritisation exercises) with no worksheets, asking, 'What would you do differently if you were faced with the same situation again?'
